notes.text: The skin of his face shone — This time of his being in the mount he heard only the same he had heard before. But he saw more of the glory of God, which having with open face beheld, he was in some measure changed into the same image. This was a great honour done to Moses, that the people might never again question his mission, or think or speak slightly of him. He carried his credentials in his very countenance, some think as long as he lived, he retained some remainders of this glory, which perhaps contributed to the vigour of his old age; that eye could not wax dim which had seen God, nor that face wrinkle which had shone with his glory.

And Aaron and the children of Israel saw it, and were afraid — It not only dazzled their eyes, but struck such an awe upon them as obliged them to retire. Probably they doubted whether it was a token of God's favour, or of his displeasure.

And Moses put a veil upon his face — This veil signified the darkness of that dispensation; the ceremonial institutions had in them much of Christ and the gospel, but a veil was drawn over it, so that the children of Israel could not distinctly and steadfastly see those good things to come which the law had a shadow of. It was beauty veiled, gold in the mine, a pearl in the shell; but thanks be to God, by the gospel, the veil is taken away from off the old testament; yet still it remains upon the hearts of those who shut their eyes against the light.

When he went before the Lord, he put off the veil — Every veil must be thrown aside when we go to present ourselves unto the Lord. This signified also, as it is explained, 2 Cor. iii, 16, that when a soul turns to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away, that with open face it may behold his glory. The great affair of setting up God's worship is now upon its former channel again. I. Moses gives Israel those instructions he had received, which required a present observance, (1.) Concerning the sabbath, ver. 1-3. (2.) Concerning the contribution that was to be made for erecting the tabernacle, ver. 4-9. (3.) Concerning the framing of the tabernacle, and the utensils of it, ver. 10-19. II. The people bring in their contributions, ver. 20-29. III. The head workmen are nominated, ver. 30-35.

glossa.text:
*And when he came down. ((ISID. in Exod., tom. V.))* Moses went up again into the mount, etc., *as far as* whose image was in the tables.

((ISID. ibid.)) When Moses came down with the tables, etc., *as far as* whence: *Open thou mine eyes, and I will consider the wondrous things of thy law ((Psal. CXVIII))*.

*But Aaron seeing,* etc. ((ORIG., hom. 12 in Exod.)) It is written that Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, etc., *as far as* for the things which he speaks have glory, but it is covered and hidden, and all his glory is within.

((ORIG. ibid.)) Consider this also, that in the law the countenance of Moses is glorified, although it be covered with a veil, etc., *as far as* that we, freed from the servitude of the world, may seek after the liberty of knowledge.

*And then he spoke to the children of Israel Isael all things which had been to him,* etc. ((AUG., quaest. 172 in Exod.)) After Moses came down from the mount, etc., *as far as* that they might receive this name.

notes.text: People — Such as are enemies to God and his people. Sitteth - Upon the ark. He is present with his people. Earth - The people of the earth. Moved - With fear and trembling.
Them — All people.

Judgment — Though his dominion be absolute, and his power irresistible, yet he manages it with righteousness. The king's strength is by a known Hebraism put for the strong, or powerful king. Equity - In all thy proceedings.
Foot-stool — Before the ark, which is so called, 1 Chron. xxviii, 2. Holy - It is consecrated to be a pledge of God's presence.
Moses — Moses before the institution of the priesthood executed that office, Exod. xxiv, 6. That call - Who used frequently and solemnly to intercede with God on the behalf of the people.
Spake — To some of them: to Moses and Aaron, Exod. xix, 24; xxxiii, 9-11; 1 Sam. vii, 9, &c.

Them — The intercessors before mentioned. Forgavest - The people for whom they prayed, so far as not to inflict that total destruction upon them which they deserved; An exhortation to praise God and to rejoice in him, ver. 1- 5 A psalm of praise This psalm was composed by David between the time of God's promising the kingdom to him and his actual possession of it. The general scope of David's vow, at his entrance on his government, ver. 1, 2. The particulars of it, ver. 3-8. A psalm of David.

glossa.text: *A psalm of David.* ((AUG.)) The prophet describes Christ the king giving good things, etc., *as far as* but the veil has been taken away, since *truth is sprung out of the earth, and justice hath looked down from heaven ((Psal. XLVIII))*. *The Lord hath reigned* ((CASS.)) Concerning the power and the kingdom of Christ, that he may be adored in the man. He shows Christ reigning, and (whosoever may resist) high above all, whence he admonishes to yield to him. *Let the peoples be angry.* ((CASS.)) A derision. It can safely be granted that they be angry, because they are not going to hurt any further: he speaks by permitting, not by commanding. *He sitteth upon the cherubim.* ((ID.)) Against him the earth can do nothing, even though he himself was on the earth where he suffered the wrath of the people. *Cherubim.* ((AUG.)) *The fulness of knowledge* is its interpretation, which is charity. The fulness of the knowledge of the law, which is the seat of God, shall be in thee also, if thou hast charity, against which the angry can do nothing. For what is the earth against heaven?

*The Lord in Sion.* ((ID.)) If thou dost not understand what is *upon the Cherubim,* see this, that he is *great in Sion.* Sion is the soul which beholds God. *Great in Sion.* ((CASS.)) Who the Lord is, he sets forth: *In Sion* born. *Great,* lest he grow cheap on account of the passion. Or, yet the Lord is great in the Sion of the Jews, and above the peoples of the Gentiles.

*Great.* ((AUG.)) It was little when they were angry, that is, made known among few, but now enlarged in all the earth. *Terrible.* ((ID.)) Because even if he is preached as crucified, he is the judge to come, and he shall not err in judgment. *And the honor of the king.* ((CASS.)) He sets forth how they ought to confess. *The honor of the king,* is the glorious preaching, *judgment* requires discernment; he is to be worshipped not with a light will, but with fixed deliberation, which is from him; whence he subjoins: *Thou hast prepared directions.* Or *the honor of the king* is the damnation of the guilty, whereby the glory of the king is increased.
*In Jacob.* ((AUG.)) Not only the patriarch, but the people whom he signifies. *Thou hast done.* These things, which another could not do.

*Exalt ye.* ((CASS.)) The second part admonishes to adore him, because his fathers *were.* As it were, because he does these things for us, therefore *Exalt ye.*

*The footstool.* ((AUG.)) *The earth is the footstool of his feet,* says Scripture, etc., *as far as* in whose honor it adores the footstool. *Of the feet.* ((CASS.)) *The feet,* the unfailing stability of the Godhead. *Holy.* That thou mayest distinguish the body from the Godhead, even though it be one person.
*Moses.* ((CASS.)) A priest, because if not victims, he offered the vows of the people, and made supplication for the people.

*A pillar.* ((CASS.)) The strength and the beauty of the house. In this appearance he spoke, which announced the Church, or the flesh, but then in a cloud, now openly through the Son: *He spoke to them out of the cloud.* ((ID.)) To them therefore then in a cloud, who now speaks to us in the footstool, that is, openly in the flesh assumed. *His testimonies and precepts.* ((ID.)) A testimony is a signification set down by certain signs of a preceding thing: whence often in the law it is said: *This shall be to you for a testimony.* The precepts are as the precepts of the law given through Moses.

*Thou wast merciful to them.* ((AUG.)) It is not said save of sins, merciful in forgiving, merciful also in avenging, behold, even though these were so great, yet they had somewhat of sin; whence he adds, *upon all their inventions.*

*Avenging.* Lest human elation should creep upon them; whence: There was given me a sting of my flesh *((II Cor. XII)) Inventions.* Otherwise, affections. ((AUG.)) Which God alone knew in their hearts; whence it was a punishment to them to bear with those among whom they were, for whose sins they grieved as for their own, through charity. For it was not, as is thought by very many, a punishment to Moses not to enter into the land of promise, into which the wretched also entered; but a figure, that they who were under the law, and were unwilling to be under grace, should not enter into rest.

notes.text: Having therefore this hope — Being fully persuaded of this.

And we do not act as Moses did, who put a veil over his face — Which is to be understood with regard to his writings also. So that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly to the end of that dispensation which is now abolished - The end of this was Christ. The whole Mosaic dispensation tended to, and terminated in, him; but the Israelites had only a dim, wavering sight of him, of whom Moses spake in an obscure, covert manner.

The same veil remaineth on their understanding unremoved — Not so much as folded back, (so the word implies,) so as to admit a little, glimmering light. On the public reading of the Old Testament - The veil is not now on the face of Moses or of his writings, but on the reading of them, and on the heart of them that believe not. Which is taken away in Christ - That is, from the heart of them that truly believe on him.

When it — Their heart. Shall turn to the Lord - To Christ, by living faith. The veil is taken away - That very moment; and they see, with the utmost clearness, how all the types and prophecies of the law are fully accomplished in him.

Now the Lord — Christ is that Spirit of the law whereof I speak, to which the letter was intended to lead. And where the Spirit of the Lord, Christ, is, there is liberty - Not the veil, the emblem of slavery. There is liberty from servile fear, liberty from the guilt and from the power of sin, liberty to behold with open face the glory of the Lord.

And, accordingly, all we that believe in him, beholding as in a glass — In the mirror of the gospel. The glory of the Lord - His glorious love. Are transformed into the same image - Into the same love. From one degree of this glory to another, in a manner worthy of his almighty Spirit. What a beautiful contrast is here! Moses saw the glory of the Lord, and it rendered his face so bright, that he covered it with a veil; Israel not being able to bear the reflected light. We behold his glory in the glass of his word, and our faces shine too; yet we veil them not, but diffuse the lustre which is continually increasing, as we fix the eye of our mind more and more steadfastly on his glory displayed in the gospel.

Therefore having this ministry — Spoken of, chap. iii, 6. As we have received mercy - Have been mercifully supported in all our trials. We faint not - We desist not in any degree from our glorious enterprise.

But have renounced — Set at open defiance. The hidden things of shame - All things which men need to hide, or to be ashamed of. Not walking in craftiness - Using no disguise, subtlety, guile. Nor privily corrupting the pure word of God - By any additions or alterations, or by attempting to accommodate it to the taste of the hearers.

glossa.text: *Having.* That is, the dignity of the New and of the Old Testament having been shown, he shows the use of each. *Much confidence.* By use we exercise ourselves in good works, whence confidence grows for us. For we shall see so much as we believe, and because the glory is open, we hide not our meaning, as Moses did, but speak openly.

*The selfsame.* Because they now understand no otherwise than before the coming of Christ. *Which is made void in Christ.* Whence in the passion of Christ the veil of the temple was rent, that it might be signified that through the passion of Christ the sacraments of the law and of prophecy are revealed. For he says a veil in comparison with prophecy, that it should not nou be understood.

*But until,* etc. For those who are in Christ it is made void: *but upon their heart there is a veil,* that is, a blindness pressing down their reason: *when,* that is, although, *there is read,* that is, expounded, to them, *Moses.* And so two things stand in the way, why they understand not, both a veil, that is, obscurity is in the reading, and blindness upon their hearts, and this even unto the present day.

*But when he shall be converted.* That is, when their mind, having laid aside the hardness of heart and its own blindness, shall have been converted by believing. *The veil shall be taken away.* So that the wine may be understood to lie hid in the water, for all prophecy, Christ not being understood, is a thing insipid and foolish.

*Now the Lord is a spirit.* The order of the words is: The Holy Spirit is Lord, that is, he can work what he wills, and therefore what he wills he enlightens; and what he wills he leaves in darkness. *But wheresoever the Spirit of the Lord is,* that is, of the Son, through whom the Holy Spirit is given, *there is liberty:* and therefore the Jews, who have not the Spirit, cannot understand freely as we do. Or, the Lord to whom they are converted is a spirit, that is, a spiritual essence, and so he makes them understand spiritually.

*We with face unveiled.* On which there is a veil for the Jews. In a mirror nothing but an image is discerned. This therefore we strive after, that through this image, that is, reason, which is what we are, we may in some sort see him by whom we were made, as through a mirror. *Into the same image.* Because the same image of God is the glory of God, as above: *The man indeed is the image of God, and the glory of God.--He is transformed.* We pass from form into form, from a dark one into a bright: because that dark image also is the image of God in which men were created, whereby they are set over the beasts. Which excelling nature, when it is justified by God, is changed from a deformed form into a comely form. For even among vices there is a good nature. Or this is understood of the glory of creation into the glory of justification. Or of the glory of faith, where we are sons of God; into the glory of sight, where we shall be like to him, when we shall see him as he is.
*Commending.* That your light may shine before men. *Before God.* Not that they may be seen by men.

notes.text: Matt. xvii, 1; Mark ix, 2.
In glory — Like Christ with whom they talked.
They saw his glory — The very same expression in which it is described by St. John, John i, 14; and by St. Peter, 2 Pet. i, 16.
A cloud came and overshadowed them all. And they, the apostles, feared, while they (Moses and Elijah) entered into the cloud, which took them away.

glossa.text: *After these words.* Others, who count only six days, signify that after the six ages of the world the saints must rest from labour. Luke, who counts in both the first day on which it is promised and the last on which the promise is fulfilled, hints that we shall rise on the eighth. For as Christ, after the sixth day of the week on which he ascended the cross, and after the seventh day of the week on which he rested in the sepulchre, rose on the eighth day, so we, after the six ages of the world in which we suffer and labour for the Lord, and after the seventh of the rest of souls which meanwhile is passed in another life, shall rise in the eighth age. *He took Peter.* He names three only, because *many are called, few chosen ((Matth. XX))*, and those who keep the faith of the Trinity inviolate deserve to rejoice in the eternal vision. He who knows merits knows that the three apostles were more perfect than the rest. They signify those who have faith, hope, charity. Or by Peter, prelates or the married; by James, the penitent or the active; by John, virgins or the contemplative.

*And he was made.* Being transfigured, he did not lose the substance of true flesh, but showed the glory either of his own or of our resurrection; and such as he then appeared to the apostles, such will he appear after the judgment to all the elect. For in the judgment itself he will appear both to the good and to the evil in the form of a servant, that they may see him whom they pierced. *And his raiment.* The Lord's garments are the saints who have put on Christ. Which garment, while the Lord dwelt on earth, seemed contemptible and like that of others, but shines when the Lord ascends the mountain, because *it hath not yet appeared what we shall be, but at length we shall be like to him, when we shall see him as he is.* Or the garments of the Word are the discourses of the Scriptures, and certain clothings of the divine understanding. Because as he himself appeared to those apostles in another form and his garment shone, so also to the eyes of thy mind the sense of the divine readings already grows white.

*Behold two men.* It is to be noted that not the bodies or the souls of Elias or Moses appeared, but that those bodies were formed out of some underlying creature: it can also be believed that this was done by angelic ministry, so that angels took upon them their persons. A dead man and a living man appear, that they may signify that Christ was to die and afterwards to live, and that we should live to Christ and die to the world. To the apostles also he gives a sign from heaven, that their faith may be increased. But to the scribes tempting him he would not give one, that they might be hardened. *And they were Moses and Elias, seen.* By Moses are signified those of the lower regions; by Elias, the heavenly; by the apostles, the earthly, who shall come to the judgment.

*They spoke of his decease.* Moses, that is the lawgiver, and Elias, the most eminent of the prophets, appear with the Word, that they may show that he is the one who spoke in the law and the prophets, and whom the law and the prophets promised. Who were seen not in the lowest places, but on the mountain, because only those lofty in mind perceive the majesty of Scripture, which was fulfilled in the Lord.

*They were heavy with sleep.* They are weighed down with sleep, because the sense of the human body is oppressed by the splendour of the incomprehensible godhead. Or they are weighed down with sleep, that they might see the glory of the resurrection after the rest of the body; and the saints will see the majesty of the Lord the more truly in proportion as they rejoice in the immortality of their flesh, in which they had conquered death. Then they shall behold Moses and Elias in glory, because they will better understand how *one iota or one tittle shall not pass from the law ((Matth. V))*, and how the Lord did not destroy the law and the prophets, but fulfilled them.

*It is good for us to be here.* He who had climbed to the mountains does not wish to descend to earthly things, but always to persevere on high; and Peter stands in the person of those entering the kingdom of God. *It is good for us to be here.* It is good to be in the kingdom of God. As if he should say: We alone shall enjoy this light, not the envious Jews. *Three tabernacles.* That is, words, thoughts, works. *One for Moses.* How do they know those whom they had not seen before? By the majesty coming upon them, as in the resurrection to come each one will know the other, and the one will understand through charity the things desired in the other.

*There came a cloud, and overshadowed them.* Although Peter is ignorant out of weakness, yet the devotion of his service pleases. Whence also the cloud overshadows; this overshadowing is of the divine Spirit, which does not darken the affections of men, but reveals hidden things, whose perfect one is shown when the voice is heard saying: *This is my Son.* Because he sought a material tabernacle, he received the shade of a cloud, that he might learn that in the resurrection the saints are to be protected not by the covering of houses, but by the glory of the Holy Spirit. *And they were afraid.* They fear, because human frailty does not endure to bear the sight of a greater glory; and by how much the greater the things a man has sought, by so much the more does he sink down to lower things, if he has been ignorant of his own measure.

*And the voice.* The voice of the Father, the terror being taken away, teaches Peter the truth. And note that, as when the Lord was baptized, so also when he was transfigured, the mystery of the Trinity is declared, because the glory which we confess in baptism we shall see in the resurrection. The Spirit in a dove, here in a bright cloud, because he who now keeps the faith with a simple heart will then contemplate in the open light of vision what he believed, and by that very grace by which he shall be illuminated he shall be protected. *Jesus was found alone.* Not Elias, not Moses, but he whom alone you see: for him the tabernacle must be fixed in the heart. They therefore withdraw when the Lord began to be pointed out, lest the Father's voice should be thought to have been sent to the servants.

echoes.text: Moses went up on the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain. Yahweh’s glory settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. The seventh day he called to Moses out of the midst of the cloud. The appearance of Yahweh’s glory was like devouring fire on the top of the mountain in the eyes of the children of Israel. Moses entered into the midst of the cloud, and went up on the mountain; and Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
echoes.note: Going up the mountain, the cloud overshadowing, the glory, the entering into the cloud, and the divine voice replay Moses' Sinai ascent. 'About eight days' may even mirror Exodus 24:16's 'six days... the seventh day.' Very high volume and coherence in Luke's new-Sinai staging.

echoes.text: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him. When Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come near him. Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him; and Moses spoke to them. […]
echoes.note: The altered, shining appearance of Jesus' face directly parallels Moses' face shining after speaking with God on the mountain. Strong verbal/visual volume; Luke uniquely heightens the facial transformation, tightening the Moses typology.

echoes.text: Yahweh your God will raise up to you a prophet from your midst, of your brothers, like me. You shall listen to him.
echoes.note: 'Listen to him' from the cloud quotes the Mosaic 'a prophet like me... him you shall heed,' identifying Jesus as the eschatological prophet-like-Moses. High volume (near-verbatim imperative) and total coherence with Moses' presence on the mount.

echoes.text: I will tell of the decree. Yahweh said to me, “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
echoes.note: 'This is my beloved Son' draws on the royal decree 'You are my Son,' fusing enthronement sonship with the Transfiguration glory. High coherence with the chapter's Christ-confession and the baptismal voice Luke echoes.

echoes.text: “Behold, my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights— I have put my Spirit on him. He will bring justice to the nations.
echoes.note: The heavenly designation of the Son in whom God delights blends the Servant 'my chosen, in whom my soul delights' with the royal Son. Moderate volume in Luke's wording; coherent with the Isaianic-Servant note already sounded in v.22.

echoes.text: “Remember the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded to him in Horeb for all Israel, even statutes and ordinances. Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of Yahweh comes.
echoes.note: Moses and Elijah standing together is precisely the Malachi pairing—'remember the law of Moses... I will send Elijah'—epitomizing the Law and the Prophets that witness to Jesus. Strong coherence; their joint appearance is unlikely to be accidental.

echoes.text: I saw until thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat: his clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was fiery flames, and its wheels burning fire.
echoes.note: The dazzling white clothing ('white as snow,' raiment 'glistering') colors the transfigured glory with the apocalyptic radiance of the Ancient of Days and heavenly beings. Moderate volume via the whiteness motif; coherent with the Danielic Son of Man already in v.26.

echoes.text: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle. Moses wasn’t able to enter into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle.
echoes.note: The overshadowing cloud from which the voice speaks recalls the glory-cloud filling the tabernacle, especially as Peter proposes building 'tents/booths' for the three. The tent/tabernacle-glory linkage gives moderate volume and good coherence.

echoes.text: He arose, and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb the Mount of God. He came there to a cave, and lodged there; and behold, Yahweh’s word came to him, and he said to him, “What are you doing here, Elijah?” He said, “I have been very jealous for Yahweh, the God of Armies; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and slain your prophets with the sword. I, even I […]
echoes.note: Elijah's own theophany on the mountain (Horeb), reached after a fast and meeting God in stillness, undergirds his presence at this mountain revelation. Moderate coherence given Elijah is literally present; volume carried by the mountain-theophany pattern.

echoes.text: It will happen that everyone who is left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up from year to year to worship the King, Yahweh of Armies, and to keep the feast of tents.
echoes.note: Peter's wish to make three 'booths' may glance at the eschatological Feast of Tabernacles when the nations keep the festival before the King. Faint and dependent on the skene wordplay; contested.

echoes.text: Yahweh went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them on their way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light, that they might go by day and by night:
echoes.note: Moses and Elijah speak of Jesus' 'exodus' he was to accomplish at Jerusalem; the very word frames the passion as a new exodus, with the guiding cloud as a faint backdrop. The 'exodus' lexeme is load-bearing but the pillar-of-cloud link is diffuse.
